title: Routing spec emulator and gradual adapter
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: We will build a routing specification emulator that runs a candidate routing configuration (new DSL or legacy config) against a synthetic traffic model to validate decisions for region selection, tier routing and fallback model variants before enabling configs in prod. The emulator will produce deterministic canonical outputs (route selection traces, fallback triggers, and cost/latency projections) which are used by a gradual adapter to translate and stage legacy policy snippets into the new policy model.

Scope:
- Emulator: deterministic simulator that accepts a policy config + traffic profile and outputs per-request route decisions, simulated latency/cost, and a compact evidence trace to aid debugging.
- Gradual adapter: transform utility that proposes staged diffs for legacy rules (legacy-region-affinity, tier priorities, fallback mappings) and emits a compatibility layer that can be enabled as a canary.
- Validation harness: a set of smoke tests, property checks (idempotence, deterministic fallback), and contract assertions (no silent drop, explicit fallback present for each model group).
- Observability: synthetic run dashboards (Grafana) and an auto-generated report (Confluence) summarizing mismatches and risky rule patterns.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full runtime enforcement hooks, long-running policy rollout orchestration, and per-tenant RBAC (separate follow-ups).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Emulator binary (or service) that can be invoked locally and via CI with a policy config and a selected traffic fixture; returns a structured evidence trace and non-zero exit code on contract violations.
2) Adapter script capable of rewriting 90% of common legacy rule forms into new DSL with a confidence score and a recommended staged-canary config.
3) CI job that runs emulator against top-10 real traffic fixtures (from anonymized production traces) and fails on high-risk rule patterns; results pushed to a dashboard and Confluence report.
4) Performance: emulator executes a 1M-request fixture in less than 60s on CI job runner (cost projection calculated), and produces memory and time profiles attached to the run.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Deterministic simulation vs probabilistic: we choose deterministic replay of synthesized request vectors so we can produce repeatable regression signals. This means we may miss rare nondeterministic interactions; we will add probabilistic fuzzing as a follow-up (see TODO).
- Adapter heuristics: the adapter will favor conservative rewrites that preserve explicit fallbacks and regional constraints. For ambiguous legacy constructs we emit a manual review flag rather than an automated rewrite.
- Performance: emulator is optimized for batch simulation over microsecond-perfect timing — it's a validation tool, not a latency profiler. For end-to-end latency SLO checks we link to the runtime perf harness.

Migration plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): deliver emulator + adapter + CI smoke. Run against sandbox tenants and internal test teams.
- Phase 2: enable canary translation for small subset of configs (platform-internal), collect telemetry, tighten adapter heuristics.
- Phase 3: allow customers to preview translated configs in Console with explicit opt-in.

Rollback plan: any adapter-suggested config must be applied as a separate config (not in-place) and toggled via canary. If discrepancies appear, we revert to previous config and file ENG follow-ups with the evidence trace attached.

Observability and artifacts:

- Initial Confluence report (auto-generated templates): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/RouterEmulator
- Grafana dashboard (sim runs): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/routing-sim
- Prototype runs (anonymized fixtures): s3://redwood-internal/routing-emulator/fixtures/
comments: 2026-02-15 - Priya Shah: Kickoff review done with runtime and infra. Agreed on deterministic simulator approach; infra to provision a CI runner with 8GB RAM for large fixtures.

2026-02-22 - Lucas Nguyen: Implemented core trace format and a first-pass deterministic engine. Local smoke shows correct fallback sequencing for synthetic fixtures. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123
2026-03-01 - Performance tests: 250k request fixture ran in 13s on the CI runner. Memory peak ~410MB. Need another optimization to meet 1M/60s target. Created micro-optimization task ENG-245679.

2026-03-04 - Security review request filed with SecOps (ticket SEC-768). Adapter doesn’t store key material and only reads policy text; SecOps asked for an explicit denylist for policy patterns that reference internal-only model tags.

2026-03-08 - Design feedback from PM (Aisha Khan): ensure the adapter surfaces human-readable rationale for every rewrite; add confidence score to outputs. Updating spec to include confidence heuristics.

2026-03-10 - Lucas Nguyen: Merged first iteration into staging branch. CI job added to run emulator against 4 anonymized fixtures nightly. Follow-up: add richer coverage for multi-region weighted routing (ENG-245680).
